user.title: Set up a heat pump
user.description:
Wärmewacht only reads existing entities and never controls the heat pump. Templates (EMS-ESP, Bosch HomeCom) found {found} heat pump(s); every entity can be changed in the next step.

Disabled entities a template would use: {disabled}. Enable them in the entity settings, wait until they report a value, then start this setup again.

data_description.name: Prefix of the entity ids.
data_description.source: A found heat pump fills in the entities; manual: pick them yourself.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: At least one mode needs a heat and an electricity meter. Electricity meters of the compressor without backup heater; the backup heater separately.

operation.name: Operation

data.aux_total: Backup heater total (only without per mode)

operation.description: For starts, short runs, defrosts and standby.

activity_parts.name: Activity from several entities
activity_parts.description: Only if the heat pump has no single activity entity. An 'on' flag wins in this order: defrost, hot water, cooling, heating. The set mode turns heating into cooling while it cools.

error.no_mode: Choose a heat and an electricity meter for at least one mode, or at least the compressor (then cycling and electricity only, no ratios).
error.energy_unit: An energy meter has no unit Wh, kWh or MWh.
error.aux_twice: Backup heater either per mode or as total, not both.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already set up.

data_description.min_electricity: Below it the ratio is unknown instead of a random value.
data_description.season_start_month: The current season is recomputed from the statistics.
data_description.aux_mild_from: Daily mean outdoor temperature from which the heat pump should heat alone.
data_description.efficiency_drop_percent: Drop of the heating ratio against the previous season at the same outdoor temperature; off again 5 points lower.
data_description.disinfection_temp: Hot water temperature from which a charge counts as thermal disinfection (DVGW W 551: 60 °C at the outlet; the storage sensor may read lower).

costs.name: Costs and gas comparison (optional)
costs.description: Every field may stay empty. Without an electricity price there are no costs; without a gas price no gas comparison; without a base price only the working prices are compared.

data_description.electricity_price: Gross price per kWh of the heat pump's electricity.
data_description.electricity_base_price: Only for a separate heat pump meter (heat pump tariff), gross per year. On the household meter leave it empty: that base price is paid anyway.
data_description.gas_price: Gross, per kWh on the gross calorific value (as on the gas bill). Boiler efficiency 0.87.
data_description.gas_base_price: Gross per year; spread over the days of a period.

data_description.design_outdoor_temp: From DIN/TS 12831-1 for your postcode (e.g. the BWP climate map). Without it the heat load is given per kelvin only.

aux_dhw_charges.name: Backup heater in hot water charges

start_after_end.message: The start must be before the end.

no_outdoor.message: This needs an outdoor temperature in the entities.

no_recorder.message: The report needs the recorder (long-term statistics).

missing_entity.title: Wärmewacht: entity missing
missing_entity.description: The heat pump {name} uses entities that no longer exist: {entities}. Renamed or removed? Choose them again under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure.

energy_unit.title: Wärmewacht: unusable unit
energy_unit.description: These energy meters of {name} report no unit Wh, kWh or MWh and are not counted: {entities}.

energy_stale.title: Wärmewacht: no new energy values
energy_stale.description: For more than 30 hours the source of {name} has written no new hourly energy values ({entities}). With myVAILLANT (mypyllant) the energy is fetched only once at load unless the option 'Seconds between energy data updates' is set: set it to 3600 to 7200 seconds, or update one of its energy sensors with an automation. Wärmewacht catches up on the missing hours as soon as they arrive.

source_changed.title: Wärmewacht: energy entities changed meaning
source_changed.description: At least one energy entity of {name} no longer measures what it was chosen for ({entities}); with myVAILLANT this happens when the cloud reorders its energy series, for example after cooling was enabled. Wärmewacht books nothing until the entities are chosen again under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure.

activity_foreign.title: Wärmewacht: activity entity without an activity
activity_foreign.description: {entities} of {name} reports values that carry no activity on this device (for ViCare E3 controllers 'ready' / 'not_ready'). Defrosts and the mode of runs stay empty. Remove the entity under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure.

flow_return_swapped.title: Wärmewacht: flow and return swapped?
flow_return_swapped.description: While heating yesterday, the flow of {name} was {spread} K colder than the return on average: {entities}. A heat pump warms the water, so the flow must be warmer. Usually the two entities are swapped in Wärmewacht (Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure) or the sensors at the heat pump. A flow sensor behind a mixing valve can also cause this. Spread and flow temperature are wrong until then. The notice disappears after a day with a normal spread.

counter_stuck.title: Wärmewacht: meter stands still
counter_stuck.description: At {name} the compressor ran for {hours} hours, but these meters did not rise: {entities}. Wärmewacht books nothing meanwhile. Check whether the source (e.g. EMS-ESP) still sends values and whether the entity is enabled. If it is the wrong meter, choose another under Devices & services → Wärmewacht → Reconfigure. The notice disappears as soon as the meter rises again.

source_unavailable.title: Wärmewacht: source unreachable
source_unavailable.description: These entities of {name} have been unavailable for more than {minutes} minutes: {entities}. Meanwhile Wärmewacht lacks values. Check the source (e.g. EMS-ESP, MQTT or Bosch HomeCom). The notice disappears as soon as values arrive again.

outdoor_temp_stuck.title: Wärmewacht: outdoor temperature unusable
outdoor_temp_stuck.description: The outdoor temperature of {name} ({entities}) has not changed for {hours} hours. Performance curve, heat load and the checks 'Efficiency dropped' and 'Backup heater on mild days' depend on it. Check the sensor or choose another entity under Reconfigure.

outdoor_temp_implausible.title: Wärmewacht: outdoor temperature unusable
outdoor_temp_implausible.description: The outdoor temperature of {name} ({entities}) was outside -35 to +45 °C for {hours} hours yesterday. Performance curve, heat load and the checks 'Efficiency dropped' and 'Backup heater on mild days' depend on it. Check the sensor or choose another entity under Reconfigure.

report.name: Report
report.description: Heat, electricity and ratios of a period, also before the setup (from the long-term statistics), with months.

start.name: Start
start.description: Without: start of the current season. Times without zone are local time.

performance_curve.name: Performance curve
performance_curve.description: Ratio per 2-K class of the daily mean outdoor temperature, without standby (at least 7 days per class).

start.name: Start
start.description: Without: start of the current season. Do not mix seasons with different heating curves.

scope.name: Scope
scope.description: Heating, or heating and hot water.

heat_load.name: Heat load
heat_load.description: Energy signature: weekly heating power over the weekly mean outdoor temperature (weeks below 12 °C).

end.name: End
end.description: Without: end of the last complete season, or now with a start.

design_outdoor_temp.name: Design outdoor temperature
design_outdoor_temp.description: Without: the one from the settings.
